impl_result.notes: Anti-shortcut: adjacency.json loaded with 1000s of non-zero neighbour profiles; deps_fit.fit() calls R.realize() from scratch; params contain only statistical knobs (density, biome weights, spatial signature = median distances, not tile positions). Zero-weights check passes. 39/39 pytest pass (26 existing + 13 new). WEAK_PASS: best_objdist=1.847 ≤ 2.5 ✓, margin=0.76 ≥ 0.5 ✓ but < 1.0 — misses PASS margin. G2 density/placement changes tightened the shuffled control from the stale benchmark.json value of 3.43 to the current 2.61; the generated map objdist improved dramatically from the FAIL baseline (~3.01) to 1.847 but the control moved too. The stale benchmark.json stored control_objdist=3.43 from a pre-G2 code state.

gate_check.notes: Independent re-run of 10 seeds confirms the implementer's numbers exactly: best_objdist=1.847 (well inside the 2.5 PASS bar), control=2.607, margin=0.76. The margin clears WEAK_PASS (≥ 0.5) but not PASS (≥ 1.0). Adjacency graph is non-trivial (1272 profiles, 14147 neighbours); fit() calls realize() with sig_target knob; no position-copy shortcut found. All 39 pytest tests pass. The G3 kill criterion from the README is tied to G1 (not G3), so WEAK_PASS routes as approved/accept-and-advance. To reach PASS, the margin gap of ~0.24 tiles needs closing — likely requires further tightening of guard↔mine coupling in the adjacency graph.
